stage: selection rule, committed before any public source is searched

selection_rule.question: Does any public cell type exist that is ABSENT from AlphaGenome's RNA track metadata as we hold it, AND has public accessibility (DNase or ATAC) and RNA-seq from the same source?
selection_rule.match_field_reason: ontology_curie is a controlled identifier shared with ENCODE, HCA and Tabula Sapiens; biosample_name is free text and a different spelling would read as absent.
selection_rule.covered_set: the distinct ontology_curie values of every row whose output == 'rna_seq' in data/cache/entex/alphagenome_track_metadata_copy.csv
selection_rule.absent: A candidate CURIE is ABSENT only when no covered CURIE is (a) equal to it, (b) an ancestor of it, or (c) a descendant of it. A child term of a covered parent is NOT absent: the parent's RNA track was trained on tissue that contains the child. A parent term of a covered child is NOT absent either: the covered cells lie inside it.
selection_rule.relation_evidence: No ontology graph is held in this repository, so the ancestor/descendant relation is not computed. Each candidate declares the covered CURIEs it is related to, with the evidence. One declared relation makes absent_by_rule False. A candidate whose relation was not checked is recorded relation_unchecked and is NOT counted absent.
selection_rule.accessibility: A DNase-seq or ATAC-seq (including scATAC-seq) experiment on the same biosample term, with processed per-region signal or peaks obtainable without an application.
selection_rule.rna: An RNA-seq experiment (bulk or single-cell with a usable pseudobulk) on the same biosample term.
selection_rule.same_source: Both experiments published by one archive or consortium under one accession family and one processing pipeline, so the pair needs no cross-archive harmonisation: e.g. two ENCODE experiments on one ENCODE biosample, or one HCA/Tabula Sapiens project carrying both modalities.
selection_rule.licence: Open access, no application, no data-use agreement, no controlled-access tier. dbGaP, EGA and any 'apply for access' resource do not qualify.
selection_rule.minimum: One cell type is enough to answer YES. Zero is NO_SOURCE_QUALIFIES.
selection_rule.acceptable_answer: NO_SOURCE_QUALIFIES is a complete answer: Albert's biosample question then closes without a lift.
selection_rule.wording_limit: The metadata file is what we hold, not what AlphaGenome saw. 'Absent from the metadata' is not 'absent from the training set'. This inventory licenses no claim about the model.
selection_rule.no_biosample: This lane adds no biosample and runs no out-of-domain test. 2026-09-27 stop list.

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record c441b90

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
